topic: Stanford-led preregistered studies (arXiv 2605.22687, May 2026, N=2,691): people expect AI to save 55.7 s on quick tasks, it saves 7.5 s; on easy tasks AI is slower; using AI raises later AI use
title: AI felt faster. The stopwatch disagreed.

source.title: The efficiency-gain illusion: People underestimate the rate of AI use and overestimate its benefits on simple tasks

body:
People guessed AI would save them 55.7 seconds on a quick task. It saved 7.5.

That gap comes from three preregistered studies of 2,691 US adults, led by researchers at Stanford and posted in May 2026.

The tasks were small. Add two numbers. Fix a typo. Find another word for "enjoy".

People guessed their own speed well: 99 seconds, against 93.7 for real. They thought AI would finish in 43.3. It took 86.2.

On the easiest tasks, AI made people slower: 70.2 seconds, against 60.2 alone. Writing the prompt took longer than reading the answer.

And the habit feeds itself. After two tasks with AI, people chose it for 44.5% of the next ones. After two tasks alone, 27.7%.

What it does not mean: that AI is slow on big jobs. Every task here took under five minutes.

This week, time one small task both ways, by hand and with AI. Keep the faster habit.

Source: Yu et al., Stanford, arXiv, May 2026 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22687

pages.headline: AI felt faster. The stopwatch said it barely was.
pages.deck: Stanford-led researchers timed 2,691 people on quick tasks, with and without AI. What people expected and what happened were far apart.

pages.label: Time people expected AI to save on a quick task
pages.body: It actually saved 7.5 seconds. Three preregistered studies, all on tasks that take under five minutes.

pages.headline: You know your own speed
pages.body: People guessed they would need 99 seconds alone. They took 93.7. Their guess with AI was 43.3 seconds. It took 86.2, nearly double.

pages.headline: The easiest tasks, timed
pages.right: 70.2 seconds. Writing the prompt took longer than reading the answer.

pages.headline: You use AI more than you think
pages.body: Asked ahead, people said they would use AI on 33% of tasks. They used it on 47%. On the easiest tasks, 20% said yes and 38% did.

pages.headline: Using it makes you reach for it again
pages.body: After two tasks with AI, people chose it for 44.5% of the next ones. After two tasks done alone, 27.7%.

pages.quote: People will use AI if they believe it to be faster.
pages.body: What it does not mean: that AI is slow on big jobs. Every task in these studies took under five minutes.

pages.label: Do this today
pages.headline: Time one small task both ways
pages.body: Pick one small task you now hand to AI. Do it once by hand and once with AI, and time both. Keep the faster habit.

pages.headline: One idea, decoded, every week
pages.body: Plain English, a named source, and one thing to do with it.

second_comment: The limits, from the paper itself: the people were US adults on a paid survey site, and every task took under five minutes. The authors say the next question is the size of task where AI really starts to save time and effort. That line is worth finding in your own work, one timed task at a time.
